finding.source: Owner-controlled request body field request.json['user'] (line 45), which adds a principal to the ACL.
finding.sink: n['shared'] list consulted by can_view (line 8) and therefore by read() via require_view (line 28).

read() still serves the note to that former sharee.

finding.guards_checked: Checked the whole file for any unshare, DELETE, PUT-on-shared, or ACL-reset route: none exists. Owner-only edit gate (line 17) is correct for granting but offers no revoke path. Duplicates are also allowed, so repeated grants grow the list without bound.

finding.claim: Note-ID existence oracle: the lookup happens before the authorization check. A nonexistent id raises KeyError and returns 500, while an existing note the caller cannot view returns 403. An unauthenticated or low-privilege caller can enumerate which note IDs exist, which matters if IDs are guessable or sequential.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled nid path parameter (line 25 route, line 26 handler).
finding.sink: NOTES[nid] lookup (line 27) and the differing responses from require_view abort(403) (line 13) versus an uncaught KeyError.

trace.note: Route /n/<nid> accepts any string as nid.
n = NOTES[nid] raises KeyError when the id is absent, giving a 500.
For an existing note, require_view runs after the lookup.
abort(403) for an existing note the caller cannot view, so the status code differs from the nonexistent case.
write() and share() (lines 34 and 43) have the same lookup-before-check ordering.

finding.guards_checked: No try/except around the lookup, no uniform 404 or 403 response, and no randomized ids are visible in this file. Impact depends on how note ids are generated, which is outside this file. Severity is low.

verdict.guard_found: none. There is no try/except around the lookup at notes.py:27 or notes.py:34, and no uniform 404 or 403 response. require_view (notes.py:11-13) runs only after the lookup at line 27 and returns 403 only for existing notes, so a missing id gives an uncaught KeyError (500) and an existing but unviewable note gives 403.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: the route at notes.py:25 takes any nid, NOTES[nid] at notes.py:27 raises KeyError before require_view at notes.py:28 runs, and abort(403) at notes.py:13 produces a different status, so a caller who can reach the route can distinguish existing from nonexistent ids. The attacker only needs to be an authenticated low-privilege user, since g.user must be set for the 403 path to be reached, and the auth setup is outside this file. Impact is a low-severity enumeration oracle that is only meaningful if ids are guessable, which this file cannot show, and the claim that unauthenticated callers can exploit it is unverified because g.user's origin is not in the code available.
